_comment: Popularity: how many people care about each club, on 0-100. This is the authored ranking, hand-set once and never derived. It replaces a hash of the club's name, which made the most popular club in the league whichever of the thirty-two names happened to hash highest.

rank.note: Position in the authored popularity list, 1 most popular. All thirty-two are distinct: there are no ties in this list, and a tie would need two clubs at the same `size` rather than two clubs at the same `rank`. `rank` is display and ordering only -- NOTHING reads it to compute an effect. `size` is the value every consumer uses.

size.note: Popularity on 0-100, and the ONLY field here that drives anything. PLACED BY RANK, EVENLY: `98 - 3 * (rank - 1)`, so 98 for the most popular club and 5 for the least, three points apart at every step. Even spacing is a choice and it is the least interesting one available: no curve, no exponent, and no club hand-tuned away from its neighbours, so the ranking in `rank` is exactly the ranking you see on screen. To make the top of the league matter more, edit the individual numbers -- the file is the data, not a formula. Measured tier spread under `checkFanbase`: major 5, large 7, mid 8, small 8, marginal 4.

_notAField.note: There is no `attendance`, no `viewership` and no `revenue` field here, and there is deliberately no formula from `size` to any of them in this file. Popularity is a property of a club; what a crowd does with it is a model, and that model belongs in `lib/` where its coefficients can be argued with rather than buried in data. The gate on all of it: `checkFanbase` asserts `size` does not correlate with `rating` or `previousBaselineWins`, because a popularity figure that tracks club quality stops being about popularity and becomes a strength proxy wearing a costume.

_fallback.note: A club absent from this file gets a hash of its own identity, exactly as before this file existed. That is not a placeholder to be filled in -- a league built from custom or imported clubs will never be in here, and `marketSizeFor` must return a number for every one of them or `liquidityFor` and `gapRiskFor` go undefined for those clubs and the price path breaks with them. `checkFanbase` asserts all thirty-two are present anyway.
